judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper addresses the problem of finding a geometrically maximal unramified abelian covering of the modular curve X0(p) over Q, unramified outside the cusps. While Mazur previously proved that the Shimura covering X2(p) -> X0(p) is the maximal unramified abelian covering, this study constructs a new cyclic covering X'2(p) -> X0(p) of degree 2Np. The authors demonstrate that this new covering is geometrically maximal when restricted to the open curve Y0(p) (X0(p) minus the cusps). The construction relies on generalized Dedekind eta functions to define a specific modular function whose square root generates the quadratic extension required to double the degree of the Shimura covering. The paper establishes that this extension is unramified outside the cusps and provides explicit conditions on the prime p for the construction. The result refines the understanding of the maximal abelian extensions of modular curves by showing that allowing ramification at the cusps permits a larger, cyclic covering of degree exactly twice the Shimura degree.

Research Context
The study focuses on maximal unramified abelian coverings of modular curves. Mazur proved the Shimura covering is maximal for the full curve X0(p). However, the full curve X0(p) includes cusps where ramification is unavoidable. Prior work established the maximal unramified subcovering of X1(p) has degree Np. The gap is whether a larger covering exists if we exclude the cusps.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is the existence of a larger maximal covering over the punctured curve. The hypothesis predicts a cyclic covering of degree 2Np exists. It is hypothesized that this new covering factors through the Shimura covering. The covering is expected to be unramified outside the cusps. The degree is predicted to be exactly double the Shimura degree.

Methodological Details
The base field for the study is the rational numbers. The modular curves X0(p) and X1(p) are treated as smooth proper curves. The cusps are defined as the complement of the open subscheme Y0(p). The divisor D consists of the two Q-rational cusps 0 and infinity. The generalized Jacobian eJ is defined with modulus D. The study utilizes the maximal torsion module MTor of the generalized Jacobian. The abelian fundamental group is related to the torsion points via duality. The construction relies on generalized Dedekind eta functions Eg. The Bernoulli polynomial B(x) is used in the definition of Eg. The study assumes p is an odd prime, with special cases for p=2,3. For p >= 5, the construction uses a generator g of (Z/pZ)×. The degree Np is defined as (p-1)/gcd(p-1, 12).

Procedures And Architectures
The function field Q(X'2(p)) is constructed as a quadratic extension. The extension is generated by the square root of a specific modular function. The modular function Fh is defined as a product of eta functions raised to a power. The exponent 6/ℓ is chosen to ensure Fh is well-defined. The group Γ'2(p) is defined as the kernel of a character involving ψ and χ. The character ψ is defined based on the parity of c and d in the matrix. The character χ is defined when ℓ is even (p ≡ 1 mod 4). The modular curve X'2(p) corresponds to the group Γ'2(p). The covering ramifies precisely at each cusp. The order of Fh^2 at any cusp is proven to be odd. The construction handles the case p ≡ 11 mod 12 separately using triplets. For p ≡ 11 mod 12, the function Gh is used instead of Fh.

Key Results
The main theorem states the existence of a cyclic covering of degree 2Np. This covering is geometrically maximal over Y0(p). The covering factors through the Shimura covering via a degree two map. The degree two map πp is unramified outside cusps. The order of the maximal torsion module is either Np or 2Np. The function Fh^2 is a modular function on X2(p) defined over Q. The order of Fh^2 at non-cusp points is zero. The order of Fh^2 at cusps is odd, ensuring ramification. The group Γ'2(p) is a normal subgroup of Γ0(p). The quotient Γ0(p)/Γ'2(p) is cyclic of order 2k. The construction works for all primes p >= 5. For p=2 or 3, a simpler map Gm -> Gm suffices.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The result implies the maximal unramified covering over Y0(p) is larger than over X0(p). The degree doubling suggests a specific structure in the Galois group. The use of eta functions provides an explicit construction of the extension. The ramification at cusps is necessary to achieve the maximal degree. The result connects the geometry of cusps to the arithmetic of the covering. The construction refines Mazur's theorem by considering the punctured curve. The cyclic nature of the covering simplifies the Galois structure.

Contradictions And Limitations
The paper assumes p is an odd prime, excluding p=2. Special handling is required for p=2 or 3. The construction for p ≡ 11 mod 12 uses a different function Gh. The explicit form of the square root depends on the choice of h. The paper assumes the existence of a degree one divisor.

Claims
The cyclic covering X'2(p) -> X0(p) of degree 2Np is geometrically maximal over Y0(p). The order of Mµ Tor(−1) is either Np or 2Np. The covering is geometrically maximal over Y0(p).  
The function Fh^2 is a modular function on X2(p) defined over Q. F 2 h is a modular function on X2(p) deﬁned over Q.  The extension is generated by the square root of Fh^2.

Data And Code Availability
The paper is a theoretical mathematical note without code or data.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The construction is robust for all primes p >= 5. The case p ≡ 11 mod 12 requires a different function Gh.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the construction of a cyclic covering of degree 2Np. 2. The strongest evidence is the proof that Fh^2 has odd order at cusps.
